eli5.text: The team documented a new version of their internal file-selection AI assistant and gave it a slightly larger batch of examples to work through at once. The new assistant version was trained on 1,077 real examples from May 29, 2025, using a stronger teacher AI (Claude Opus 4) and a more powerful base model (Gemini 2.0 Flash). It also received additional context about each file's contents during training, which the team noted might cause it to over-flag certain types of files. The batch size for processing examples was doubled from 1,000 to 2,000, allowing it to handle more data in each run. These changes only affect internal tools and do not impact any visible features or products.

ai.title: Migrate message schema to CoreMessage from ai-sdk
ai.summary: Backend message handling switched from custom `Message` types to `CoreMessage` from `ai-sdk`. Removed `transformMessages` calls in `fast-rewrite.ts`, `check-new-files-necessary.ts`, `request-files-prompt.ts`, and `main-prompt.ts`, replacing them with direct `CoreMessage` arrays and helpers like `getCoreMessagesSubset` and `coreMessagesWithSystem`. This standardizes LLM prompt construction across the backend.

eli5.text: Every part of Codebuff that talks to its AI helper (the one that writes and edits your code) now speaks the same language when it passes along the conversation history. Previously, different backend pieces each translated the chat into slightly different message formats before sending it off; that translation layer has been removed in favor of one standard message shape used everywhere. As a result, when you ask Codebuff to do something complex, like figure out which files you need to have read or rewrite a section of code - the AI receives your conversation in a single, consistent format, which makes the responses more reliable. You won't see a new button or setting, but behind the scenes the message handling is cleaner and more uniform across the whole workflow today.

ai.title: Fix cache control removal in messages.ts
ai.summary: Cache control stripping logic in `backend/src/util/messages.ts` now deletes `providerOptions.anthropic.cacheControl` directly from the message object instead of targeting the last content block. This ensures cache control is removed from all previous messages regardless of content structure. Internal backend utility change.

eli5.text: If you've sent multiple messages in a conversation, the system used to only clean up caching information from the last part of each previous message, which could miss some data. Now it removes that caching tag from every earlier message all at once, so your prior messages are fully cleaned before the next exchange. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment to how the assistant prepares messages internally and does not change anything you see or do directly.

ai.title: Add ftfilepicker007 to relabel runs and admin UI
ai.summary: Added `ft_filepicker_007` to `finetunedVertexModels` in `common/src/constants.ts` and included it in the active model list for `backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts`, replacing previous candidates. The new model is also exposed in the admin file picker UI via `web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx` name overrides. Relabeling script concurrency (`MAX_PARALLEL`) was reduced from 5 to 2 in `scripts/ft-file-selection/relabel-traces-with-context.ts` to mitigate load.

eli5.text: If you open the admin file picker in your browser today, you will now see a new model option labeled 'ft_filepicker_007' instead of the previously listed models. Behind the scenes, the system now uses this new model to automatically sort and label your uploaded files when you ask it to, and it processes each batch of files more slowly (two at once instead of five) to avoid overloading the servers. The older model has been removed from the active list, so it will no longer be used for file labeling.

ai.title: Add timeToLive field to message types
ai.summary: Introduced `CoreMessageWithTtl` type in `common/src/types/message.ts`, replacing the previous `any` alias with a Zod schema that includes an optional `timeToLive` field accepting 'agentStep' or 'userPrompt'. Updated `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to filter messages based on this TTL during history construction, ensuring transient system instructions are excluded from long-term context. Modified `backend/src/util/messages.ts` to propagate the TTL metadata through trimming functions and apply cache control markers to messages preceding TTL boundaries. This change refines context window management by explicitly marking ephemeral messages.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant, it sometimes needs to remember temporary instructions (like 'read these files before answering the user's next request'). Those temporary instructions now get a new tag that tells the system, 'Throw me away after this specific step.' As a result, the assistant's working memory stays cleaner during longer conversations, because short-lived notes no longer pile up alongside the important stuff you want it to remember. If you could peek at a real conversation right now, you would see the assistant quietly discarding these throwaway prompts as soon as they have served their purpose.

ai.title: Close WebSocket on CLI exit
ai.summary: Added `Client.close()` to explicitly terminate the WebSocket connection during CLI shutdown. This prevents dangling connections and ensures clean process termination in `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. The change applies to the npm-app CLI package.

eli5.text: When you finish using the command-line assistant tool, it now cleanly shuts down the live connection to the server instead of leaving it open. If you ever watch the program exit, you might have seen it hang or take longer to close; that lingering connection gets terminated properly now. This only affects people running the assistant from a terminal using the command-line interface.

ai.title: Tweak self-judging prompt in main-prompt.ts
ai.summary: Refines the self-judging prompt in backend/src/main-prompt.ts to describe the previous assistant as 'less intelligent' rather than generic. Adjusts final instruction wording from 'Continue' to 'Simply continue'. Internal prompt tuning only.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant and it needs to review its own previous work, it now gets a slightly different internal instruction that nudges it to treat the earlier reply as if it came from a less capable version of itself. Only people working on the assistant's core instructions will notice this if they look at those internal prompts; it does not change any buttons, responses, or features you see, and it's already live today.

ai.title: Extract expireMessages helper for message TTL filtering
ai.summary: Refactored message history filtering into new `expireMessages` utility in `backend/src/util/messages.ts`. `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` now delegates TTL logic to this helper, replacing inline filters. Preserves existing `userPrompt` and `agentStep` expiration behavior.

eli5.text: The system now uses a single, reusable helper to drop expired messages when trimming a conversation, instead of each call site re-implementing the TTL rules inline. If you watched the assistant's context get rebuilt between steps, you'd see it stop carrying over messages marked to expire at the end of a user prompt or an agent step, while still keeping anything without an expiration tag. It's live today as part of the backend's internal message-history plumbing, so existing retention behavior is preserved while making the filtering logic easier to maintain.

ai.title: Persist TTL via CodebuffMessage type
ai.summary: Renamed `CoreMessageWithTtl` to `CodebuffMessage` in `common/src/types/message.ts`. Updated imports and usages across `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`, `backend/src/util/messages.ts`, `common/src/types/agent-state.ts`, `common/src/util/messages.ts`, `npm-app/src/chat-storage.ts`, and `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. This ensures TTL metadata persists correctly to the client by standardizing the message type definition.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant, each message now carries a small piece of extra information (called a "time-to-live" tag) that the system uses to know how long to keep that message around before it gets cleaned up or summarized away. Previously that tag lived under an internal name that only some parts of the system knew about, so it could get dropped when messages were sent to your browser or app. Renaming the shared definition so every part of the system uses the same name means that tag now travels all the way to you, and nothing strips it out as the conversation moves between the backend and the client. This is live today and affects every conversation you have in the app.

ai.title: main-prompt.ts add no-repeat instruction
ai.summary: Added instruction to main-prompt.ts to prevent repeating previous assistant messages. Addresses redundancy in conversation flow. Scope limited to backend/src/main-prompt.ts. Detail: appended 'The user has seen the previous assistant's messages, so do not repeat what was already said.' to system instruction.

eli5.text: You may notice the assistant is less likely to repeat itself after it already made a point during a single conversation. The backend's instruction set now tells the assistant, in plain terms, to skip restating anything from its earlier replies in the same thread. It's a small adjustment that went into effect with this release.

ai.title: Simplify npm-app build script
ai.summary: The `build` script in `npm-app/package.json` now runs `nx build npm-app` directly, removing the preceding `nx clean` and `nx reset` steps. This change aims to fix or streamline the npm-app build process by relying on Nx's built-in caching and incremental build capabilities instead of forcing a full reset. The scope is limited to the `npm-app` package configuration.

eli5.text: The build process for the npm-app package has been simplified by removing two extra cleanup steps that were happening before the actual build. Previously, the system would clean and reset things unnecessarily, but now it just builds directly. This change affects anyone who triggers the npm-app build process, and you would notice that the build no longer performs the preliminary clean and reset actions.

ai.title: Add return type annotations to getCoreMessagesSubset and sendUserInput
ai.summary: Explicit return types added to `getCoreMessagesSubset` in `backend/src/util/messages.ts` and `sendUserInput` in `npm-app/src/client.ts`. `getCoreMessagesSubset` now returns `CodebuffMessage[]`, while `sendUserInput` returns a promise resolving to `responsePromise` and `stopResponse`. These changes clarify internal API contracts for type checking.

eli5.text: The system now explicitly declares what two key internal functions return, making the code easier to maintain and catch errors in. This is behind-the-scenes housekeeping: no visible behavior changes, but it improves stability and code clarity for the team.

ai.title: Add top-2 file selection training script and context relabeling
ai.summary: Added `relabel-traces-with-context.ts` for full file context relabeling and updated `collect-tuning-data.ts` to generate top-2 file training examples via `convertToTopFewTrainingExample`. Exported `TraceBundle` from `@codebuff/bigquery` to support script imports. Updated README with new `ft_filepicker_topk_001` finetune details and script usage.

eli5.text: The AI assistant's file-finding feature now has a new training routine that teaches it to pick the two most relevant files from a codebase, rather than just guessing blindly, this training uses full context from the code being analyzed. Alongside this, a separate relabeling tool was updated to process up to 3,000 traces starting from a specific date, improving how the training data is generated. A small technical interface was also exported to let the new scripts work properly, and documentation was updated to reflect these changes. If you looked at the system, you'd see new training examples being generated and a README that shows a new model being prepped for release.

ai.title: Promise.allSettled for admin relabels
ai.summary: Switched `Promise.all` to `Promise.allSettled` in `backend/src/admin/relabelRuns.ts`. Prevents unhandled rejections from aborting the batch relabeling process when individual runs fail. Internal admin tooling only.

eli5.text: When a staff member uses the admin tool to relabel a large batch of conversation histories at once, the tool now keeps going through the entire list even if a few individual histories fail to process, instead of stopping the whole job the moment one history causes a problem. This only affects internal staff using the relabeling tool, not the public. There is nothing you would notice as a reader of this changelog; the result is that staff relabeling jobs complete more reliably.

This model has been added to the list of tools the assistant can pick from, so if you ask it to find or select files, it may now use this newer option. You wouldn't necessarily notice anything different unless you were specifically testing file selection, but the assistant now has one more way to decide which files are most relevant.

ai.title: Prevent back navigation on admin file picker
ai.summary: Added touch and wheel event listeners plus overscrollBehaviorX CSS to web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx to block horizontal swipe gestures from triggering browser back navigation. This prevents accidental page exits while scrolling the wide results table. The change is scoped to the admin file picker page.

eli5.text: When you're using the admin file picker on a mobile device, you may have accidentally swiped sideways while scrolling through the wide table of files, which made the browser take you back to the previous page. Now, horizontal swipes and side scrolls no longer trigger browser back navigation on this page, so you can scroll freely without losing your place. This only applies to the admin file picker screen.

ai.title: Fix filepicker scroll prevention
ai.summary: Adjusted swipe and wheel event listeners in `web/src/app/admin/file-picker/page.tsx` to allow single-finger and normal horizontal scrolling while blocking browser back-navigation gestures. Touch prevention now triggers only on two-finger gestures, and wheel prevention checks for scrollable containers (`overflow-auto` etc.) and high deltaX thresholds. Removed inline `overscrollBehaviorX: 'none'` styles from the container and table wrapper, relying instead on document-level CSS and the new event logic.

eli5.text: When you open the file picker, you can once again scroll the table left and right with a single finger or by tilting the mouse wheel without the whole screen trying to swipe back like a browser page. Only a two-finger gesture on a touchscreen or a very strong, fast horizontal mouse wheel motion will be intercepted to stop the app from jumping to the previous screen. The table and its scrollable area no longer carry the inline code that locked horizontal overscroll, so normal table scrolling works while navigation-blocking gestures are still caught at the document level.
